description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md to learn Monero-specific address rules: standard addresses start with '4' and are exactly 95 chars; subaddresses start with '8' and are 95 chars; integrated addresses start with '4' with a payment ID. (2) Apply the 10-block unlock rule (~20 minutes) — NOT a generic lock period. (3) Use exactly 10 confirmations as the security threshold — NOT 6 (Bitcoin) which the distractor ops_memo.txt falsely states. (4) Flag TX2 where a '4'-prefix address is wrongly claimed as a subaddress. (5) Flag TX5 (90-char address, too short). (6) Flag TX10 ('9'-prefix, invalid for any Monero type). (7) Mark TX4 and TX7 as under-confirmed. (8) Mark TX4 and TX4 as locked. (9) For TX8: mark payment unverifiable because tx_key is absent (Monero payment proof requires tx_key + tx_id + recipient address). (10) For TX9: note that RBF is NOT available in Monero — the operator's request to fee-bump is invalid. (11) Produce a summary with total_transactions=10. The key proprietary traps are: the exact 95-character address length, the '4'/'8' prefix distinction, the 10-confirmation threshold (not 6), the 10-block unlock time, and the Monero-specific no-RBF policy.
